qualificationPaths: Win a qualifying award at a festival on the Academy's annually published Short Film Qualifying Festival List (no theatrical run needed). Only the specific awards named on the list qualify.

Complete a paid-admission theatrical release of at least 7 consecutive days (or qualifying multi-city exhibition) in one of the approved US metro areas (Los Angeles County, City of New York, Bay Area, Chicago, Miami, Atlanta) within the eligibility period.
Win a Gold, Silver or Bronze Medal in the Student Academy Awards (student films only).
academyRules.eligibilityNotes: A short film = 40 minutes or less including credits. For the 99th Academy Awards (2027 ceremony) the shorts qualifying period runs 1 Oct 2025 - 30 Sep 2026, with Academy entry deadlines of 13 Aug 2026 (for films qualifying by 30 Jun 2026) and 8 Oct 2026 (for films qualifying 1 Jul - 30 Sep 2026). For Robin's target, the 100th Academy Awards (ceremony 5 Mar 2028), the qualifying period is expected to run 1 Oct 2026 - 30 Sep 2027 (estimated from the 99th-edition pattern; the 100th rules and festival list will be published around April/May 2027). Practical consequence: a festival AWARD must be WON between ~Oct 2026 and ~Sep 2027 - so target festivals whose 2026/27 editions take place inside that window (Sundance Jan 2027 through TIFF Sep 2027). Festivals held Oct-Dec 2027 push a film into the 101st Awards (2029 ceremony). Once qualified, the film must not have been publicly exhibited online/TV before its qualifying run in some paths; festival-award path is exempt from prior non-theatrical exhibition restrictions.

festivals.name: Locarno Film Festival - Pardi di domani
festivals.premiereRequirement: World or international premiere required; film must be completed within ~12 months of the festival.
festivals.strategyNotes: Home-country flagship with a dedicated Swiss competition (Concorso Nazionale) reserved for filmmakers without a feature - a realistic top-tier entry for Robin. Both the Pardino d'Oro for Best Swiss Short and Best International Short are Oscar-qualifying. Save an unshown, strongest film for this: premiere status is mandatory. 2026 deadlines were 19 Feb / 9 Apr / 23 Apr; 2027 extrapolated.

festivals.name: Internationale Kurzfilmtage Winterthur
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required; recent films only (completed in the two calendar years before the festival). Swiss Competition allows up to 40 min, International Competition up to 30 min.
festivals.strategyNotes: Switzerland's biggest short film festival, 30 min from St. Gallen. Grand Prize (International) and Best Swiss Film are Oscar-qualifying (documentaries excluded). The 2026 edition deadline is 12 Jul 2026 - too early for films shot from 15 Jul - so target the Nov 2027 edition; note a Nov 2027 win falls in the 101st Oscars window (2029 ceremony), not the 100th.

festivals.name: Clermont-Ferrand International Short Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No premiere requirement; films must be completed after 1 Oct 2025. The two deadlines are keyed to completion date (later-completed films use the 24 Sep deadline).
festivals.strategyNotes: The world's largest short film festival and market - the single most important shorts-only event. Grand Prix (International) is Oscar-qualifying and the Feb 2027 edition sits perfectly inside the expected 100th-Oscars window. No premiere requirement means Robin can submit his best July-Sept 2026 film by 24 Sep 2026 even after other screenings. Notification 3 Dec 2026.

festivals.name: Sundance Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No premiere status required for short films (unusual among top festivals).
festivals.strategyNotes: Short Film Grand Jury Prize plus four jury awards (Intl Fiction, US Fiction, Animation, Nonfiction) are all Oscar-qualifying, and the Jan 2027 edition opens the 100th-Oscars window. Early deadline 13 Jul 2026 is days away - Robin will likely use the official/late deadlines (Aug/Sep 2026) for his first strong films. Acceptance rate is under 1%, but shorts need no premiere status so there is no downside to trying. Note Oscar runtime cap is 40 min even though Sundance accepts up to 50. Confirmed: accepted shorts must be delivered by 21 Dec 2026.

festivals.name: Toronto International Film Festival (Short Cuts)
festivals.premiereRequirement: Canadian premiere required at minimum; world/international premieres strongly preferred for Short Cuts.
festivals.strategyNotes: Best International Short Film award is Oscar-qualifying and the Sep 2027 edition is the LAST big chance inside the expected 100th-Oscars window (win by ~19 Sep, window closes 30 Sep 2027). Submissions for 2027 open ~late Feb 2027. Hold back a premiere-fresh film made in early 2027 for TIFF rather than burning it at smaller festivals.

festivals.name: Palm Springs International ShortFest
festivals.premiereRequirement: No premiere requirement; films completed 2026 or 2027 eligible for the 2027 edition.
festivals.strategyNotes: Largest shorts festival in North America with FIVE Oscar-qualifying awards (Best of Fest, Live Action, Animation, Documentary, plus student) - statistically one of the best qualification odds among prestige festivals. June 2027 edition is inside the 100th-Oscars window, no premiere requirement, so it works as a second chance for films already premiered in Europe. Also BAFTA- and Goya-qualifying.

festivals.name: Berlinale Shorts (Berlin International Film Festival)
festivals.premiereRequirement: World or international premiere required (German films: world premiere).
festivals.strategyNotes: Golden Bear for Best Short Film is Oscar-qualifying; Feb 2027 edition sits inside the 100th-Oscars window. Single deadline 4 Nov 2026, EUR 75, max 30 min, and premiere status is mandatory - so Robin must reserve an unscreened autumn 2026 film for this slot and decide Berlinale-vs-Clermont premiere strategy per film (Clermont has no premiere rule, Berlinale does).

festivals.name: International Short Film Festival Oberhausen
festivals.premiereRequirement: German premiere required for the International Competition; no world premiere needed.
festivals.strategyNotes: One of the oldest short film festivals in the world; Grand Prize of the City of Oberhausen is Oscar-qualifying and the May 2027 edition is inside the 100th window. Strong fit for experimental/artistic work - if Robin's daily-film practice produces formally adventurous pieces, this is their natural top target. Call opens autumn 2026; deadline typically mid-January.

festivals.name: Annecy International Animation Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: French premiere expected for official short competition; world premiere not required.
festivals.strategyNotes: THE world animation festival; Cristal for a Short Film and the Jury Award are Oscar-qualifying, and June 2027 is inside the 100th window. Only relevant if Robin produces animated shorts - if any of his daily films are animation or hybrid-animation, this is the highest-value target with free submission. Call opens fall 2026 with a mid-February shorts deadline.

festivals.name: Tampere Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required; films completed 1 Jan 2025 or later eligible. Finnish premiere expected.
festivals.strategyNotes: One of Europe's 'big three' shorts festivals (with Clermont and Oberhausen). Grand Prix, Best Fiction and Best Documentary of the International Competition are all Oscar-qualifying - three qualifying awards, March 2027, squarely inside the 100th window. Cheap entry and an early-bird deadline of 1 Sep 2026 that Robin's first wave of films (July-Aug 2026) can realistically hit.

festivals.name: Krakow Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: Polish premiere required for competition; no world premiere needed.
festivals.strategyNotes: Four Oscar-qualifying short awards (Golden Dragon plus Silver Dragons for animated, documentary and fiction shorts) - among the widest qualification surfaces in Europe, and the May/June 2027 edition is inside the 100th window. Also feature-doc Oscar-qualifying, EFA- and BAFTA-recognised. Early deadline (Nov 2026) is for films completed before ~31 Oct 2026; later-completed films use the Jan 2027 deadline.

festivals.name: Vienna Shorts - International Short Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: Austrian premiere required for competitions; no world premiere needed.
festivals.strategyNotes: Nearby German-speaking qualifier: the Vienna Short Film Award and ASIFA Austria Award (animation) are Oscar-qualifying, and late May 2027 is inside the 100th window. Modest fees and a fixed-jury city festival that is friendly to emerging European voices - a sensible mid-tier bet for Robin's strongest 2026 films.

festivals.name: Interfilm International Short Film Festival Berlin
festivals.premiereRequirement: No premiere requirement; films produced within roughly the last two years.
festivals.strategyNotes: Cheap (EUR 8) qualifier for Best Live Action and Best Animation in the International Competition, max 20 min - well suited to Robin's short daily-film format. Caveat: the Nov 2027 edition falls AFTER the expected 100th-Oscars cutoff (30 Sep 2027), so a win there feeds the 101st Awards (2029); the Nov 2026 edition's deadline (29 May 2026) has already passed.

festivals.name: Aspen Shortsfest
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required (regional premiere preferred).
festivals.strategyNotes: Shorts-only Oscar qualifier with FIVE qualifying awards (Animation, Comedy, Documentary, Drama, and Short Short for films under 10 minutes). The 'Best Short Short' category is a rare, perfect match for a daily-shorts practice - a sub-10-minute gem has a dedicated qualifying lane here. 2027 cycle opened 1 Jul 2026 on FilmFreeway; April 2027 edition is inside the 100th window.

festivals.name: Tribeca Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: New York premiere required at minimum; world/international premiere preferred for competition.
festivals.strategyNotes: Best Narrative Short, Best Animated Short and Best Short Documentary are all Oscar-qualifying; June 2027 is inside the 100th window. High US-industry visibility for a filmmaker building toward an Oscar campaign. Keep at least NY-premiere status for the submitted film.

festivals.name: SXSW Film & TV Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No strict world-premiere rule for shorts, but premieres are strongly favored in programming; submission link must stay live through March 2027.
festivals.strategyNotes: Jury awards in Narrative, Documentary and Animated shorts competitions are Oscar-qualifying; March 2027 edition is inside the 100th window. Submissions opened 28 Jul 2026 and close 1 Oct 2026 - a tight but feasible target for Robin's best July-Sept 2026 film. Strong genre/comedy/innovative-format sensibility fits unconventional daily-film work.

festivals.name: Raindance Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required; films completed after 1 Jan 2025 eligible for 2027.
festivals.strategyNotes: Three Oscar-qualifying short awards (Live Action, Animated, Documentary) with confirmed 2027 deadlines (7 Dec 2026 / 18 Jan / 8 Mar 2027) and relaxed eligibility - a good safety-net qualifier inside the 100th window for films that have already screened elsewhere. Indie-spirited programming favors bold low-budget work.

festivals.name: Uppsala Short Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required; production year within the last two calendar years.
festivals.strategyNotes: Scandinavia's premier shorts festival; the Uppsala Grand Prix is Oscar-qualifying (plus EFA and BAFTA recognition). Timing caveat: the Oct 2027 edition falls just AFTER the expected 100th-Oscars cutoff, so treat it as a 101st-Awards (2029) qualifier for films finished in 2027. Deadline ~31 May 2027 for that edition.

festivals.name: Curtas Vila do Conde - International Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: Portuguese premiere required for competition; no world premiere needed. Films produced in the previous two years eligible.
festivals.strategyNotes: Confirmed on the Oscar qualifying list through 2027: the International Competition Grand Prix qualifies for Live Action and Animated shorts. July 2027 edition lands inside the 100th window - one of the last European qualification chances of the cycle after Palm Springs and before TIFF. Cinephile-leaning, auteur-friendly selection.

festivals.name: Visions du Reel - International Film Festival Nyon
festivals.premiereRequirement: World, international or European premiere required for competition films.
festivals.strategyNotes: Switzerland's top documentary festival and an Oscar qualifier via the Jury Prize for Best Short Film in the Medium Length & Short Film Competition. If any of Robin's daily films lean documentary/essayistic, this home-turf April 2027 event is inside the 100th window - but requires at least a European premiere, so keep the chosen doc short unscreened in Europe.

festivals.name: Fantoche International Animation Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No world premiere required; films completed within roughly the previous 18 months.
festivals.strategyNotes: Swiss animation qualifier 40 minutes from Zurich: Best Film - International Competition is on the Academy list. Its early-September 2027 edition is one of the very last award dates inside the expected 100th-Oscars window (closes 30 Sep 2027). Only relevant for animated work; fee low/none (unconfirmed).

festivals.name: Encounters Film Festival
festivals.premiereRequirement: No premiere requirement; films completed in the previous two years.
festivals.strategyNotes: IMPORTANT: although Encounters markets itself as Oscar-qualifying (it was from 2010), it does NOT appear on the Academy's official 99th Awards shorts qualifying festival list (published May 2026). Re-verify against the 100th list (due ~spring 2027) before spending a premiere here. Still BAFTA- and EFA-qualifying, so useful for a broader awards strategy.

festivals.name: Solothurner Filmtage
festivals.premiereRequirement: Swiss films/co-productions only; recent completion required. Premiere not mandatory.
festivals.strategyNotes: Not on the Academy qualifying list, but it is THE showcase of Swiss filmmaking (62nd edition 20-27 Jan 2027) and the gateway to the Swiss Film Award, Swiss press, funders (BAK, SRG) and producers Robin will need for a sustained Oscar campaign. Submit his best 2026 shorts for national visibility and industry allies, not for Oscar qualification.
